The core insight of dynamic network tuning lies in feedback-driven adaptation where each agent modifies its local connections based on global performance indicators. This process resembles a stochastic optimization problem where the objective function is defined implicitly by the system's emergent properties—such as connectivity and modularity. The feedback loop ensures that high-performing configurations are reinforced, while low-performing ones are pruned. In GSI, this translates into Bayesian updating of adjacency matrix beliefs, where prior distributions encode expected agent behaviors. In GSE, it manifests as state transitions governed by conformal prediction intervals that ensure safety margins during reconfiguration. The failure mode arises when feedback delays exceed coherence times, leading to oscillations or divergence in network structure.
